title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 189
paragraphs: It would appear too that the Hellenes modeled the dress and aegis of the images of Athena after the Libyan women. For except that the Libyan women's clothing is of leather, and the tassels hanging from their aegis are not formed of serpents but of leather thongs, in every other respect Athena is dressed like them. Moreover, the name itself shows that the dress of the Pallas figures came from Libya, for the Libyan women wear over their other garments bare goatskins (aigeai) with tasseled fringes, colored with red madder, and from the name of these goatskins the Hellenes formed the name aegis. I think too that in these parts first arose the practice of crying aloud during sacred rites, for the Libyan women do this very well. The Hellenes also learned from the Libyans the yoking of four horses together.
